issue.title: [Bug] Windows (NTFS) 下读取 Cursor 会话引发天量磁盘写穿（单日累计写 >480GB / 读 >500GB）导致系统假死
issue.body:
### 问题描述
在 Windows 11 环境下，`magpie-windows-amd64.exe` (v0.1.1318) 伴随界面与后台正常运行时，产生了极其高频的磁盘 I/O 读写吞吐量。进程在半天内累计写入达到 **479 GB**、读取达到 **501 GB**，直接导致固态硬盘（尤其是 DRAM-less / QLC 盘，如 Crucial P2）的 SLC 模拟缓存彻底耗尽，C 盘持续 100% 占用并引发整机严重假死几分钟。

同时 Windows 系统事件日志中记录了由极端 I/O 引起的连锁故障：
- `Volsnap Event ID 25`: The shadow copies of volume C: were deleted because the shadow copy storage could not grow in time. Consider reducing the IO load on the system...

### 根本原因排查与溯源
该现象与 #1988 中讨论的 Cursor 会话读取机制直接相关：
1. 本机 Cursor 的全局存储数据库 `AppData\Roaming\Cursor\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb` 体积较大（约 **8.72 GB**）。
2. 在 #1988 的修复中，macOS 端改用了 APFS 的文件系统克隆（Copy-on-Write），因此不会产生额外的物理磁盘写入与高昂开销。
3. 但在 **Windows (NTFS)** 环境下，由于没有 APFS 类似的快速克隆机制，magpie 在进行会话扫描或定时同步时，若继续执行文件级完整复制或无索引全量扫描，对一个 8.72 GB 的数据库只需扫描数十次，磁盘读写量就会轻松被放大到 **400GB ~ 500GB+**，对 Windows 用户（特别是系统盘安装在常规消费级 SSD 上的用户）造成巨大的 I/O 冲击与寿命磨损。

### 环境信息
- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit (NTFS 文件系统)
- **magpie 版本**: v0.1.1318 (`magpie-windows-amd64.exe gui agents`)
- **Cursor 数据库大小**: `state.vscdb` 约 8.72 GB
- **硬件影响**: 触发 DRAM-less SSD I/O 队列打满，系统盘 100% 锁死

### 建议与期望
1. **Windows 适配优化**：避免在 Windows 上对整个数 GB 甚至十几 GB 的 `state.vscdb` 进行物理副本拷贝。例如通过 SQLite 原生以只读模式（`mode=ro` 或 `immutable=1` URI 参数）在原文件上并发只读，或者利用 Windows 的只读文件共享句柄直接读取。
2. **安全阈值与配置开关**：对单文件体积设置上限（如超过 1GB 则跳过物理复制），或提供设置项允许用户关闭 Cursor 历史会话发现。

comments.body:
原因和你的判断一致：Cursor 运行时 state.vscdb 旁边有活动 -wal，magpie 每次读取都走"把库和 -wal 复制一份"的路径（internal/sessions/cursor.go:226）。16 MB 以上的库共享一份副本，而这份副本在 APFS 上是 clonefile、不占空间；在 NTFS 和 Linux 上 cloneFile 直接返回 ErrUnsupported，于是退回 copyFile（internal/sessions/cursor_snapshot.go:134），库或 -wal 一变就把整个数 GB 文件重写一遍。Cursor 一直在写，所以一次列表、一次统计、一个 transcript、一次搜索都是一份完整拷贝。

分支改成：库和 -wal 合计达到阈值的库不再复制，直接在原文件上以只读模式（mode=ro）打开，最新消息从 -wal 读取；读取只会在库旁边写入 SQLite 的读标记（-shm，一到两页），也就是你建议的 mode=ro 方案。小于阈值的库仍然复制，保证 Cursor 目录不被写入；就地打开失败时仍退回复制。所有读取其它应用 WAL 库的路径都经过同一个 OpenUntouched，所以 Cursor CLI 会话、编辑器历史、Pi Desktop 标题、aionui/Cindy/NewMax 一并修好。

你建议的第 2 条没有做："超过 1 GB 跳过复制"的效果等同于这次的就地只读读取，"关闭 Cursor 历史发现"的开关是产品选项，没有加。

[fix/3228-windows-ntfs-cursor-480gb-500gb](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3228-windows-ntfs-cursor-480gb-500gb), commit ad2b0ce

验证：新增 TestCursorLargeStoreIsReadInPlace —— 拿掉改动后失败（"a live state.vscdb was copied 1 times, want 0"），改动后通过；它的 fixture 不 checkpoint，所有行只在 -wal 里，能列出会话说明日志确实被读到，同时临时目录为空。新增 TestCursorSmallStoreCopiedAndRemoved 确认小库仍复制一次、读完删除、Cursor 目录不变。go test ./internal/sessions/ -count=1 全绿（670 passed），TestCursor -race -count=3 通过；go build ./...、go vet ./internal/sessions/（含 GOOS=windows 与 nogui）通过。真实检查：沙箱 HOME 里 4 KB 的 state.vscdb 加 36 MB 活动 -wal、另一进程每 200 ms 写一行，改动前的二进制跑一次 magpie sessions --json 就写出 38 MB 副本，改动后的二进制列出全部 20 个会话且临时目录为空。

未在真实 Windows 上运行：读取在各平台都是同一个 mode=ro 打开方式，Windows 的 vet/build 通过，但没有 Windows 机器验证。这是 fork 分支，供 review，不主张该 issue 的归属。

issue.title: [Performance / 流程] 希望加上性能 CI 门禁，并给长期反馈留一条有人工看的通道

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 背景

我是 magpie 的长期用户，最近一直在提 issue（#2003、#2131、#2147、#2438、#2440）。magpie 是常驻后台、一直开着的基础软件。我还是希望它越来越好，因为同类的几个软件用起来更麻烦。所以这次想提两件比单个 bug 更长期的事：**性能回归没有门禁**，以及**用户的长期意见很难传到开发者那里**。

## 一、性能没有 CI 门禁，回归会直接发到用户手上

### 现象

- 最近几个版本里，CPU 占用时不时冲到 **130% 左右**（多核合计）。对一个常驻后台的软件来说，我觉得能吃到 25% 就已经很多了。
- 磁盘读写也明显偏高。下面是我在空闲时用系统接口读到的一次数据：

| 项目 | 数值 |
| --- | --- |
| 版本 | magpie v0.1.2563（macOS app） |
| 系统 | macOS 27.0.1，Apple M1 Pro（10 核） |
| 主进程运行时长 | 约 33 分 38 秒 |
| 主进程累计 CPU 时间 | 39.0 秒（平均约 1.9%） |
| 采样时的瞬时 CPU（`top`，每 5 秒一次，共 7 次） | 0.0%–0.7%（当时空闲，没有请求经过） |
| 主进程累计磁盘读 / 写（`proc_pid_rusage`） | **约 1181 MB 读 / 约 137 MB 写**（约 34 分钟内） |
| 插件宿主 magpie-bun 累计磁盘读 / 写 | 约 32 MB / 约 0.1 MB |
| 常驻内存 | 主进程约 179 MB，magpie-bun 约 43 MB |

> 说明：这次采样时正好碰上空闲状态，没抓到 130% 的尖峰。空闲时半小时读了 1 GB 多的磁盘，我觉得也不太正常。

### 问题在哪

看 `.github/workflows/test.yml`，CI 现在跑 gofmt、vet、单元测试、race 和几个平台测试，**但没有任何基准测试或资源用量检查**。所以一次改动让 CPU 或 IO 变高了，CI 发现不了，下一个自动版本就直接到了用户手上。仓库里已经有很多性能 issue，几乎都是用户自己用 profile 抓出来的，比如 #1665、#3394、#3228、#4293、#4353、#4366–#4372、#4735、#4737、#4742。每次都是"用户发现 → 修一处 → 再发版"，同类回归还是会反复出现。

### 具体建议

1. **CI 里加一个性能 job**，用固定的测试数据（比如一份真实规模的会话目录和 usage 日志）跑几个典型场景：冷启动、空闲 N 分钟、持续有请求经过、打开 Usage / Routing 页。记录这几项：
   - CPU 时间（总量和空闲时每分钟）
   - 磁盘读 / 写字节数
   - 常驻内存峰值
   - 分配次数 / GC 占比（Go 基准测试的 `-benchmem` 就能拿到）
2. **设阈值**：和 main 的基线比，超过一定比例（比如 +20%）就让 CI 失败，或者至少在提交上标红，让人看一眼再发版。
3. **给空闲状态定一个资源预算**，比如空闲时平均 CPU < 1%、每分钟磁盘读写不超过若干 MB，写进文档和测试里。
4. **在 release notes 里附上关键性能数字**（和上一个版本对比），用户也能自己判断要不要升级。

我想请作者认同一点：作为一个长期在电脑后台运行的基础软件，**性能和功能应该同样重要**。新功能加得很快，这是好事，但如果每隔几个版本就要靠用户去抓 profile，长期下来很伤用户的信任。

## 二、用户的长期意见很难传到开发者那里

这一点我想说得直接一些，但没有任何指责的意思，只是作为一个一直在提反馈的用户的真实感受：

- **issue 好像主要由机器人处理，而且只做"点状修复"。**我指出的具体问题，通常很快就有一个修复和一条回复，这点很好。但涉及设计或长期方向的建议，常常没有回应。比如我在 #2438 提的设备级配置同步，还附了 fork 上可以单独测试的第一步提交，从 10-15 到现在没有任何回复。
- **PR 只对协作者开放。**我自己修好了问题也没法提交，只能在本地维护一份私人构建。`docs/contributors.md` 里说可以把修复放在 fork 的分支上、贴进 issue，由 agent 合并。但这条路是否有人工评审、什么样的修复会被采纳，从外面完全看不出来，也没法像 PR 那样来回讨论。
- 结果就是：用户能报"哪里坏了"，但很难让开发者听到"这个方向应该怎么走"。这次的性能门禁就是一个例子，它解决不了单个 bug，所以很可能不会被机器人处理。

### 希望的改进

1. **给设计 / 长期反馈一个有人工看的通道**：比如一个专门的标签（如 `needs-maintainer` / `design`），或者打开 GitHub Discussions 里的一个分类，并说明维护者会定期看、会给出接受或不接受的结论。
2. **给外部贡献者一条明确的提交修复的路**：比如有条件地对外开放 PR（先过 `docs/contributors.md` 里的安全检查），或者把"fork 分支 + issue"的流程写进 README / CONTRIBUTING，说清楚谁会看、多久会有答复。
3. **这个 issue 本身**，希望能有一位人工维护者看一下，给一个是否会做性能门禁的结论。

谢谢作者做了这么好用的工具，也希望它能长期走得更稳。

---

issue.title: pii: a masking-cache save rewrites the whole `found-*.bin` and fsyncs it, ~17 GB a day on a busy gateway

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Short version.** `internal/pii` keeps what the local masking model learned in `<cache>/astrlink-guard/found-<model>.bin`. Every answer schedules a save `2 s` later, and a save encodes **the whole 20 000-entry LRU**, writes it to a temp file, `Sync()`s it, and renames it over the old one. On a gateway taking ordinary agent traffic that is **34 whole-file rewrites in 120 s — 29.7 MB over a 915 KB cache, 17–21 GB/day** — for a cache whose content changes by under a hundred bytes between saves. On this machine it landed on a 4.41 ms HDD and the box stalled; see "Why it matters".

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26300), `magpie-windows-amd64.exe` **v0.1.3990**, portable (`data\` beside the exe).
- A 13th-gen Intel i7, 16 GB RAM.
- The portable folder was on a **spinning disk** (a Storage Spaces simple volume over a SATA HDD, `Avg. Disk sec/Transfer` ≈ 4.4 ms). Moving the same install to an NVMe (≈ 0.14 ms) cleared the stall, which is what pointed at I/O in the first place.
- Code read at `main` `d370bef9`; the write path is unchanged since `27b4f412` (2026-10-26, when find/cache/download were split into a backend of their own) and a rebase check against `5eac086` found nothing newer.

## Measured

Three independent runs on an otherwise idle machine; the first two are stat-only (mtime + size), no instrumentation.

**Run A — 121 s, the `found-*.bin` of the installed model (≈ 915 KB)**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Rewrites in 121 s | 34 |
| Bytes written | 29.7 MB |
| File-size change across the run | < 100 B |
| Inter-save gaps | 4.4, 3.7, 2.7, 2.8, 2.7, 2.3, 2.3, 2.1, **12.4**, 2.2, 2.3, 4.4, 4.3, 2.2, 3.1, 2.8, 2.8, 2.5, 2.2, 3.5, 2.2, 4.1, **2.0**, 5.2, 6.9, 2.0, 3.4, 4.2, 7.5, 2.1, 6.3, 2.5, 2.5 s |
| Derived | **20.7 GB/day** |

**Run B — 301 s, three caches observed together**

| file | size | rewrites | bytes written | derived |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `cache/astrlink-guard/found-*.bin` | 916 667 | **70** | 64 166 690 | **17.13 GB/day** |
| `quota-history.json` | 672 683 | 23 | 15 471 709 | 4.13 GB/day |
| `cache/sessions.json` | 2 670 525 | 2 | 5 341 050 | 1.43 GB/day |
| **total** | | | **84 979 449** | **22.69 GB/day** |

**Run C — 182 s, file layer and OS counters read at the same time**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Rewrites | 41 × 918 620 B = 35.9 MB → **16.68 GB/day** |
| `\LogicalDisk(F:)\Disk Write Bytes/sec` (all processes) | avg 1 601 KB/s, peak 10 945 KB/s |
| `\Process(magpie-windows-amd64)\IO Write Bytes/sec` | avg 696 KB/s, peak 2 013 KB/s |

The three runs agree to within a few GB/day, and the OS counter for the process matches the file-layer figure: 16.68 GB/day ÷ 86 400 s = **202 KB/s**, against 696 KB/s measured for the whole process (which also carries the two other caches, the gateway's own append log, and its network I/O). Nothing here depends on how the file was stat'd.

For contrast, the caches that only append grew **193.7 MB/day** over the same 300 s window (`usage.jsonl` 16.3, `routing/*.jsonl` 170.3, `masking/*.jsonl` 7.1 MB/day). So the whole-file handlers write **~117×** what the data actually grows by.

Two details that rule out "append seen as rewrite":

- `fsutil file queryfileid` changed across a save (`0x…<old>` → `0x…<new>`) while the size moved 93 B: it is `CreateTemp` + `Rename`, not an in-place append.
- The file's header declares **20 000 entries** (`magic` `pfound02`, then a LE `uint32` count) — the LRU is at its cap (`internal/pii/find.go:843`, `newLRU(20000)`), so every save re-encodes all 917 KB of it no matter which one entry changed.

Cross-check at the OS layer: `\LogicalDisk(F:)\Disk Write Bytes/sec` averaged **782 KB/s** during run B (all processes), against the 275 KB/s the 22.69 GB/day figure implies for magpie alone. `magpie-windows-amd64`'s own `\Process\IO Write Bytes/sec` was ~760 KB/s in the same minutes. Run C repeated this with both layers sampled together and got the same agreement (202 KB/s implied vs 696 KB/s for the whole process, which carries the other two caches as well).

## Source-level cause

`internal/pii/find.go:269` — after a classify answer lands in the cache, every time:

```go
b.cache.put(k, got[k])
…
b.saveSoon()
```

`internal/pii/cache.go:39` and `:83-97` — and `saveSoon` arms one `saveAfter` timer:

```go
var saveAfter = 2 * time.Second
…
disk.timer = time.AfterFunc(saveAfter, func() { … bk.saveCache() })
```

`internal/pii/cache.go:103-129` — the save itself:

```go
cache.mu.Lock()
b := encodeCache(cache)   // :108 — the whole LRU
cache.mu.Unlock()
f, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(p), "found-*.tmp")  // :111
_, err = f.Write(b)
if err == nil {
    err = f.Sync()        // :117 — fsync on every save
}
…
err = os.Rename(f.Name(), p)  // :123
```

`encodeCache` (`internal/pii/cache.go:134`) walks `c.ll.Back()` to the front and writes every entry's hash, its spans and its labels. There is no dirty tracking, no delta, no size bound beyond the LRU's 20 000 entries, and no backoff: **the debounce is 2 s and the write is O(cache), so a gateway answering requests every few seconds writes the entire cache every few seconds.**

The gaps above show the shape: most land at 2.0–2.3 s (the timer firing as soon as it is armed, because there is always another answer), the longer ones (6–12 s) are the stretches where no request arrived. That is exactly "a write for a burst of requests" turning into "a write per request burst".

The other two rows of run B are the same pattern in different packages:

- `internal/provider/quota_history.go:111-131` — `writeQuotaHist` → `writeFileAtomic` → `steady.WriteFile`, which `Sync`s (`internal/steady/steady.go:159-175`). `noteQuotaHistory` (`:303`) calls it at `:372` whenever a reading changed, so the whole file is re-encoded and fsynced per changed reading. Points are deduplicated (`quotaHistGap` 5 min, `quotaHistSame` 30 s, `:46-47`) and the file capped at 6 000 points (`quotaHistMax`, `:45`), but nothing coalesces the *writes*: 23 saves in 301 s for a 672 KB file. If this should be a separate issue it can be split — it is here because it is the same shape and was measured together.
- `internal/sessions/sessions.go:1410` — `CachePath()` = `sessions.json`, rewritten whole (`:1516`); this is the file #5440 explicitly leaves open ("the `sessions.json` half of the issue remains open").

## Why it matters (and why it went unnoticed)

A cache of a few hundred KB ought to be noise. Here it is **17 GB/day of 900 KB rewrites, each followed by an fsync**, on a machine that is otherwise idle. What pushed it over the edge on this box was the medium: the portable install was on an HDD whose average transfer was 4.41 ms, and the same install on an NVMe (0.14 ms) is quiet. Anyone with `/home` or their portable folder on a spinning disk, a QLC/DRAM-less SSD, or a network share will feel the same thing; see #3228 for the Windows/NTFS version of this failure mode and #1988/#4938 for the disk pressure on macOS.

It also interacts with #5254: under sustained large-context traffic the model's catch-up never drains, `defaultWait` (`internal/masking/masking.go:179`) expires on nearly every request, and each of those expiries still lands answers in the cache — so the busiest hours are precisely the ones that save the most.

On this box the gateway logs `masking: the local model read N of M texts in 2s (stopped waiting …)` roughly every 60 s during normal work, which is a good "am I in the expensive state" signal:

```
2026/11/13 14:34:24 masking: the local model read 217 of a request's 363 texts in 2s …
2026/11/13 14:36:29 masking: the local model read 249 of a request's 400 texts in 2s …
```

## Reproduction

Stat-only, no debug build, ~2 minutes:

```bash
# 1. find the cache the running magpie is using
ls -l ~/.cache/magpie/astrlink-guard/        # or <portable>/data/cache/astrlink-guard/
# 2. have an agent work through the gateway with masking on (redact + redactModelName set)
# 3. watch the inode and the bytes
watch -n0.5 'stat -c "%i %s %y" ~/.cache/magpie/astrlink-guard/found-*.bin'   # Linux
#   Windows: fsutil file queryfileid <file>; (Get-Item <file>).Length
```

Each inode change is one whole-file save. Compare `count × size` against the file's size growth — the ratio should be two or three orders of magnitude, and it is what this issue reports.

A Go-level regression case would be: warm the cache, then call `saveSoon` (or run `find`) with one new entry every 100 ms for 10 s, and assert that the **bytes written** stayed within a small multiple of the cache size, not one full encode per debounce window. `internal/pii` already has `saveAfter` as a `var` and `disk.saves` as a `WaitGroup`, so a test can drive the timer directly.

## Possible directions

1. **Append, don't replace.** The file is already a sequence of fixed-layout entries (`magic`, count, then each entry's hash + spans). An append-only journal with a periodic full compaction would make the common path proportional to what was learned, not to the cache. A `pfound03` magic with a compaction threshold would be a natural follow-on; the reader already rejects a short/cut file and falls back to asking the model (`loadCache`, `cache.go:69-72`).
2. **Drop `Sync()`.** This is a rebuildable cache keyed by a model's answers. `#4276`'s conclusion applies here too: atomic replace is worth keeping, a per-save fsync is not. `internal/usage/log_disk.go:51` already bounds its own rewrites to `10 * time.Minute`; a similar bound here (or a "save at most once per N seconds / per M new entries") would cut this by two orders of magnitude on its own.
3. **Make the interval scale with the cache.** `saveAfter` is a constant 2 s regardless of whether the cache is 5 KB or 1 MB. `saveAfter × max(1, len(cache)/1000)` would keep a small cache snappy and a full one quiet.
4. **Bound the file.** 20 000 entries are always kept, so the save is always ~900 KB even when the process has just started and nothing changed; a smaller cap, or an idle-eviction of spans, would help the first case.
5. While here: the same whole-file-plus-`Sync` shape in `internal/provider/quota_history.go:111` and `internal/sessions`'s `sessions.json` (`#5440`'s open half) deserves the same treatment.

## Notes

- No request bodies, prompts or account identifiers are involved: the cache stores a text's sha256 and where the model found something, never the text (`internal/pii/cache.go:20-33`).
- Config: masking on with the default `astrlink-guard` (`redact: true`, `redactModelName: "astrlink-guard"`, `redactModelAuto: true`), gateway serving several agents (Codex, Claude Code, dsh) at once.
- **Workaround, not a fix:** turning the local model off (`redactModelOff: true`) stops `Find` from running, so this writer disappears; the rules-based masking is unaffected. Moving the portable folder to an SSD also removes the stall, which is what this reporter did to get the machine usable again.
- Related and distinct: #4276 and #5440 both report whole-file cache saves (the request cache and `sessions.json`). This is a third writer, in `internal/pii`, that neither issue names; #5440's fix touches `request_page.go` and its own comment says the `sessions.json` half stays open.
